newsitem.title: USA: First half U.S. copper production/deliveries rise.
newsitem.headline: First half U.S. copper production/deliveries rise.

text.p: Refined copper production and deliveries in the United States and the rest of the world rose in the first seven months of the year, the American Bureau of Metal Statistics said.

U.S. refined copper production rose to 995,100 short tons compared to 952,100 short tons in the same period last year. Production in July rose to 174,000 tons from 155,000 tons in June and 152,300 tons in July 1995.
Total first half world refined copper production, including the U.S., rose to 3,853,600 short tons, up from 3,616,900 tons in the same period last year.

Deliveries of refined copper in the U.S. in January through July rose to 1,155,800 short tons, up from 1,043,500 tons in the same period in 1995. Deliveries in July fell to 157,200 tons from a revised 194,800 tons in June.
Global deliveries rose to 3,787,200 short tons in the first half of the year, up from 3,680,000 tons in the first half of 19955.
Inventories of refined metal held by U.S. refineries at the end of July were 47,000 short tons, up from a revised 34,000 tons in June.
The ABMS said world refinery and exchange inventories totaled 1,012,900 short tons at the end of June, up from 768,700 tons at the end of June 1995, and a revised 1,047,000 tons in May 1996.
